definition: Self-authenticating documents are considered authentic and require no extrinsic evidence of authenticity to be admitted in a legal proceeding. These documents are recognized by law as having inherent reliability and credibility due to their nature or the manner in which they were created. Under Rule 902(a) of the Federal Rules of Evidence, an exception exists for a select group of documents where no authentication is required for admissibility as evidence. Specific categories include:  Acknowledged documents (documents that are notarized or sworn under oath);  Newspapers or magazines;  Trade inscriptions;  Commercial papers or documents; and  Public records or official records with proper certification.
